items.quote: At that time Sibbekai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha. In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan
items.contrast: Sibbekai is the killer in the first-described battle at Gob, whereas Elhanan is the killer in the subsequently described “another battle.”
items.reason: Elhanan is a plausible alternative because both men kill someone in battles at Gob. The passage presents Sibbekai first, but it does not explicitly establish that his battle occurred first chronologically. Thus “who kills first?” is materially ambiguous between first in time and first mentioned. A bounded rewrite such as “Who is named first as killing someone in the battles at Gob?” would make the key unique. The target is meaningful because the reader must match two killers to the order of two distinct battle accounts.
